[h1] Asteroids ++ [/h1] [h3] Pros: [/h3] [b]🚀 Classic Arcade Fun [/b] Asteroids ++ brings back the nostalgic charm of classic arcade games. It’s a straightforward space shooter that pays homage to the original Asteroids while adding a few modern twists. The fast-paced gameplay and simple controls make it easy to jump in and start blasting away asteroids. 🚀🕹️ [b]🌀 Modernized Graphics [/b] The game features updated visuals that retain the essence of the original while providing a fresher look. The neon colors and sleek designs make for a visually appealing experience that enhances the classic gameplay without losing its retro feel. 🌀🌟 [h3] Cons: [/h3] [b]🔄 Repetitive Gameplay [/b] While the game stays true to its arcade roots, the gameplay can become repetitive after a while. There isn’t much variety in the objectives or enemies, which might make it feel monotonous over time. 🔄♻️ [b]🔧 Lack of Depth [/b] Asteroids ++ doesn’t offer much in terms of content or depth. Once you’ve played a few rounds, you’ve pretty much seen everything the game has to offer. This lack of progression or new challenges can make the game feel shallow. 🔧📉 [h3] Other Drawbacks: [/h3] [b]🎮 Basic Controls [/b] The controls, while simple, can feel a bit too basic. There’s not much room for skill or strategy, which could limit the long-term appeal for more experienced gamers looking for a challenge. 🎮⬇️ [b]🌌 Minimal Upgrades [/b] The game doesn’t offer many upgrades or power-ups, which could have added some excitement and variety. The minimal customization options might leave players wanting more from the experience. 🌌🔋 [b]Good Points[/b] [list] [*]Classic arcade fun. [*]Modernized graphics. [/list] [b]Bad Points[/b] [list] [*]Repetitive gameplay. [*]Lack of depth. [*]Basic controls. [*]Minimal upgrades. [/list] [table] [tr] [th]Category[/th] [th]Score[/th] [/tr] [tr] [td]Graphics[/td] [td]⭐⭐⭐[/td] [/tr] [tr] [td]Gameplay[/td] [td]⭐⭐[/td] [/tr] [tr] [td]Sound[/td] [td]⭐⭐⭐[/td] [/tr] [tr] [td]Content[/td] [td]⭐⭐[/td] [/tr] [tr] [td]Overall Rating[/td] [td]⭐⭐⭐[/td] [/tr] [/table] [b]Personal Comment[/b] Asteroids ++ is a fun, albeit simplistic, throwback to the classic arcade days. It’s perfect for quick bursts of play when you’re in the mood for some mindless asteroid blasting. However, the lack of depth, repetitive gameplay, and minimal upgrades might make it a short-lived experience for those seeking something more engaging. If you’re a fan of retro games, it’s worth checking out, but don’t expect much beyond the basics.

Simply put. This is an updated version of the 70's classic arcade game, with tons of interactive features. In Asteroids ++ you're given a story to save the solar system by individually visiting the 8 planets and stopping their impending destruction! Once you've completed the main story, you will visit the forgotten Pluto for another rounds of missions. As you progress through the game, you collect money that you will use to upgrade your ship to become more powerful in destroying the dreaded asteroids. There are tons of upgrades to choose from, such as lasers, clones, shields, and shotguns (so choose wisely)!

Asteroids ++ is an unabashed, lazy ripoff of Asteroids (Copyright Atari, 1979). Many lazy "amateur" developers don't pay attention to their obligations under copyright law, and often steal the ideas of actual, real game developers without credit, such as the "developer" here has done. At this stage no legal action has been taken by Atari against the "developer" here, but it's never off the table, as previous copyright law cases have shown (Tetris Holding LLC vs Xao Inc in New Jersey comes to mind as one such legal precedent). And, doubling down on this, the developer is also infringing Atari's trademark. For profit. If you listen carefully you can hear the lawyers waking from their slumber already. You can't just steal someone else's game idea for profit. Copyright exists for a reason and when developers hamfistedly steal the work of others, it harms all of us. Putting aside the unethical intellectual bankruptcy of stealing someone else's game concept for profit, this is also breaking that unwritten law of stealing other people's game ideas... you should at least try to do better than the game you're ripping off. Asteroids ++ is considerably worse than Asteroids. On the upside, the game does feature customisable controls and resolution, so at least some of the basic, minimum requirements have been met. Unfortunately there's a number of other technical defects and shortcomings which contribute to the game being difficult to recommend to gamers. The game features somewhat lazy, simplistic "retro" looking 2D graphics, and it's hard to say if this is due to the age of the assets used, if it's a deliberate attempt for the game to look bad/retro on purpose, or if the assets are just, well, terrible looking. Considering this is being evaluated as a PC game in 2025, such poor quality 2D graphics in the 3D era just aren't good enough, whether it's a deliberate design fault on behalf of the developer or they just couldn't manage to do any better, this is a compromise gamers shouldn't have to put up with. These technical defects push this game below acceptable standards for any modern PC game. The game isn't really free as the developers have infested the game with a cash shop, and you're expected to fork over huge amounts of money for access to both basic game systems that are needed to play and to unlock additional content... the developer here stole Atari's game and wants YOUR money for it. Utterly reprehensible.

Asteroids ++ is a single player game based on the classic arcade game but with a variety of skills and weapons purchasable between battles. Each battle occurs in a zone which consists of multiple waves. Each planet consists of multiple zones and when all zones for a planet are won, the planet is liberated. You can configure a variety of load outs, albeit you'll discover quite quickly that certain weapons and perks are much better than others. Difficulty scales appropriately. The sound and music is of acceptable quality. Infiland currently only has this game and The Colorful Creature available on Steam. While I can't attest to the quality of the latter, this game is a fun and fresh take on the arcade classic. If you're into 2D classic arcade games, roguelikes, and 2D space combat games, this title likely offers something for you. 87% of the 89 reviews for this game are positive. The negative reviews are mostly from when the game was launched when it still had advertisements and many bugs. Out of the 8 negative reviews in English, 3 complain about bugs and/or crashes, 2 complain about ads, and the other 3 have a combined playtime of 0.4 hours with either reviews that make no sense or complain about the game being boring or low effort. For an Asteroids-based game, it's pretty good. It's a solid recommend for those seeking such a title. Especially since it is free. SCORE: 4/5 - Recommend

Asteroids ++, developed and published by Infiland, takes one of gaming’s oldest arcade concepts and rebuilds it into something much larger than a simple retro recreation. Inspired by classic space shooters but expanded with progression systems, customization mechanics, procedural generation, and long-term replayability, the game transforms familiar asteroid-blasting gameplay into a modern arcade experience built around experimentation and continuous growth. Instead of relying purely on nostalgia, it uses classic foundations as a starting point before layering modern systems that encourage players to keep improving, adapting, and discovering new ways to play. The premise establishes a science fiction backdrop designed to support progression without overwhelming players with heavy storytelling. Humanity has expanded beyond Earth and established itself further across space, only for catastrophe to disrupt stability throughout the solar system. Massive asteroid threats begin appearing after a large-scale disaster sends dangerous debris into populated regions. Players step into the role of a pilot tasked with helping restore order by traveling between locations and eliminating threats before larger consequences unfold. While narrative remains secondary to gameplay, it provides enough structure to give progression purpose. Missions feel connected to a larger objective rather than existing as disconnected score challenges. Planetary exploration and combat encounters become part of an ongoing effort to restore stability across dangerous sectors of space, helping strengthen immersion without slowing momentum. Combat remains the heart of the experience. Movement feels immediate and responsive, preserving the arcade foundation that inspired the project while allowing complexity to emerge naturally through progression. Asteroids split apart into smaller hazards, enemy encounters increase pressure, and later situations require stronger awareness than simply firing continuously. The core mechanics remain approachable while creating opportunities for mastery over time. One of the strongest features comes through ship customization systems. Rather than forcing players into predefined playstyles, Asteroids ++ encourages experimentation by offering extensive build variety. Weapons, abilities, movement options, and defensive systems can dramatically change how combat unfolds. Some players may create highly aggressive builds focused on overwhelming damage output, while others may prioritize survivability or mobility. That flexibility helps prevent progression from becoming repetitive. The ability to adjust equipment and create different strategies gives players reasons to revisit familiar challenges with entirely different approaches. Experimentation becomes rewarding because combat behavior changes noticeably depending on chosen upgrades and equipment combinations. The progression structure also supports long-term engagement effectively. Unlockable content steadily expands possibilities over time, creating a satisfying sense of advancement beyond simple score chasing. New systems and additional tools reinforce improvement while encouraging continued play sessions. The game clearly understands that modern arcade experiences often benefit from stronger progression hooks than older classics originally offered. Procedural generation strengthens replayability further. Environments and encounter structures avoid becoming overly predictable because repeated runs continue introducing variation. Players adapt to changing situations rather than memorizing fixed patterns completely. This procedural approach helps maintain freshness while supporting the game's roguelike elements. Enemy variety contributes positively to pacing as well. Different threats gradually introduce greater challenge while encouraging players to refine strategies continuously. Combat remains engaging because encounters evolve alongside player progression rather than remaining mechanically static throughout longer sessions. Visually, Asteroids ++ embraces simplicity in a way that supports gameplay clarity effectively. Space environments remain readable during intense combat situations, allowing players to focus on threats and movement without unnecessary visual clutter. Effects emphasize gameplay visibility while still providing enough impact to make combat feel energetic and satisfying. The independent nature of the project becomes visible throughout presentation, but much of the game's appeal comes from systems design rather than production scale. Infiland prioritizes mechanical depth and replayability over cinematic storytelling or visual spectacle. That design philosophy works well because the gameplay loop remains strong enough to support long-term investment. The free-to-play structure also lowers entry barriers significantly. Players can experience extensive progression systems and build experimentation without major commitment, helping broaden accessibility while reinforcing replay value. Its arcade roots naturally shape audience expectations. Players looking for heavily narrative-driven experiences may find stronger emphasis placed on gameplay systems and progression loops instead. Likewise, players who enjoy experimenting with builds and gradually mastering mechanics will likely connect more strongly with what Asteroids ++ offers. What allows the game to stand out is how effectively it balances retro inspiration with modern design ideas. Rather than simply recreating a familiar formula with updated visuals, Asteroids ++ expands its foundation into something that feels both nostalgic and contemporary. Asteroids ++ succeeds because it respects arcade history without becoming trapped by it. Infiland builds a space shooter focused on customization, progression, and replayability while preserving the fast-paced action that made classic arcade experiences memorable in the first place. For players who enjoy arcade shooters, science fiction combat, and progression systems built around experimentation and long-term improvement, Asteroids ++ delivers an entertaining modern interpretation of a timeless genre. Rating: 8/10
